headline: Mild and dry through Saturday in Kentucky before late-Sunday showers; a coastal low brings the Upstate a cooler, breezier Saturday with a limited rain chance
disclaimer: Independent amateur analysis. This is not an official forecast or warning. Follow the National Weather Service and local authorities during hazardous weather.

refresh.workflow: Update and commit forecast.json once. GitHub Actions automatically locks the prior issue in forecast-history.json. Then verify the GitHub Pages URL; every Google Sites embed reads the same file and refreshes automatically.

kentucky.name: Central Kentucky
kentucky.subtitle: Danville primary · Lexington comparison
kentucky.summary: A surface high over West Virginia and a midlevel ridge maintain subsidence, a dry column and abundant sunshine through Saturday. As the high shifts northeast, light easterly flow turns southerly and keeps afternoon temperatures near 70°F. Height falls and a shortwave flatten the ridge Sunday; increasing clouds precede a cold front, but dry sub-cloud air should delay most showers until Sunday evening and limit rainfall.
kentucky.currentConditions: At 8:15 AM EST, KDVK reported 36°F with a 34°F dew point, calm wind, clear sky and visibility above 10 miles. At 7:54 AM, KLEX reported 39°F with a 35°F dew point, calm wind and clear sky. No official NWS point alert was active for Danville at the final issuance check.

days.label: Friday / Friday night
days.hazard: OFFICIAL NWS ALERT STATUS: no active point alert covers Danville at issuance. No widespread hazardous weather is expected. Independent concerns are low afternoon humidity and localized frost in the coldest rural valleys late tonight; light wind limits fire-spread potential.
days.forecast: Sunny and mild, with only thin cirrus at times and a most-likely Danville high near 67°F. East wind remains light at 3–7 mph. Clear sky continues tonight with a most-likely Saturday-morning low near 39°F and colder valleys in the middle 30s. Widespread fog or a widespread freeze is not expected.

days.label: Saturday / Saturday night
days.hazard: No official NWS point alert covers Saturday at issuance. Independent concern is very low afternoon humidity, with grass or brush-fire spread possible; light wind keeps the concern below a red-flag presentation. Rain and thunder are not expected.
days.forecast: Sunny and unusually mild with a most-likely high near 70°F. Southeast to south wind stays around 3–8 mph. Mostly clear conditions early Saturday night give way to increasing high clouds late, but the dry column should evaporate any early sprinkles. The most-likely Sunday-morning low is near 42°F, with colder eastern valleys in the upper 30s.

days.label: Sunday / early Monday
days.hazard: No official NWS point alert covers Sunday at issuance. Independent concern is a band of showers and a brief gusty wind shift with the cold front Sunday evening or night. Rainfall should generally remain below 0.10 inch; flooding, severe storms and hazardous wind are not expected.
days.forecast: Most daylight hours remain dry. Sunshine fades behind increasing high and midlevel cloud, with a most-likely high near 68°F and south wind around 5–10 mph. A west-to-east band of gusty showers is favored from about 7 PM–1 AM EST, plus or minus three hours, then tapers before dawn. The most-likely overnight low is near 44°F before colder air deepens Monday.

kentucky.bottomLine: Central Kentucky stays sunny, dry and mild through Saturday. Most-likely Danville high/low pairs are 67/39°F, 70/42°F and 68/44°F. Sunday is dry for most daytime plans, then a narrow band of generally light, briefly gusty showers crosses Sunday evening or night. Sharply cooler air follows Monday.
kentucky.confidence: High Friday and Saturday; moderate-high Sunday because the front is well supported but exact shower onset and coverage depend on how quickly the dry column moistens

upstate.name: Upstate South Carolina
upstate.subtitle: Clemson primary · Central/Pickens County comparison
upstate.summary: High pressure north of the Carolinas maintains northeast flow while a subtropical or tropical low organizes near the Southeast coast. Increasing clouds and a shallow cool wedge trim Saturday temperatures. Clemson and Central lie on the system's western fringe, so the forecast favors only a limited late-Saturday-night or early-Sunday shower chance before the wedge weakens and temperatures recover.
upstate.currentConditions: At 8 AM EST, KCEU reported 49°F with a 38°F dew point, north wind near 6 mph, clear sky and visibility above 10 miles. KLQK was near 40°F with a 38°F dew point and light northeast wind; KGSP was 44°F with a 35°F dew point and north wind near 8 mph. No official NWS point alert was active. Tempest data was not used.

days.label: Friday / Friday night
days.hazard: OFFICIAL NWS ALERT STATUS: no active point alert covers Clemson or Central at issuance. Independent concern is very low afternoon humidity and modest fire-spread potential, but wind remains below critical criteria. Rain, thunder and a freeze are not forecast.
days.forecast: Partly sunny and mild with a most-likely corridor high near 70°F. Northeast wind runs 4–9 mph. Clouds thicken tonight and gusts may reach 18–23 mph. Most-likely Saturday-morning lows are near 52°F at KCEU and 46°F at KLQK, preserving the observed Clemson–Central split.

days.label: Saturday / Saturday night
days.hazard: No official NWS point alert covers Saturday at issuance. Independent concerns are northeast gusts around 20–25 mph and a limited shower chance late Saturday night. A farther-west coastal track would mean cooler, wetter conditions.
days.forecast: Mostly cloudy and cooler beneath strengthening northeast flow, with a most-likely corridor high near 64°F. Sustained wind runs 8–14 mph with gusts of 20–25 mph. The coastal rain shield should remain mainly east through the day, but a few light showers may reach Clemson and Central after sunset or midnight. Most-likely overnight lows are near 55°F at KCEU and 50°F at KLQK.

days.label: Sunday / Sunday night
days.hazard: No official NWS point alert covers Sunday at issuance. Independent concern is residual coastal-low track uncertainty early. Brief light rain is possible, but the favored western-fringe solution keeps heavy rain, flooding, thunder and hazardous wind east of Clemson and Central.
days.forecast: A brief light shower remains possible early, followed by decreasing clouds as the coastal low lifts north and northeast and the shallow wedge erodes. The most-likely corridor high is near 69°F, though a farther-west low track would remain cooler and wetter. North to northwest wind becomes light. Most-likely Sunday-night lows are near 50°F at KCEU and 45°F at KLQK.

upstate.bottomLine: The Upstate is mild and dry today, then cooler, cloudier and breezier Saturday. Most-likely corridor highs are 70°F, 64°F and 69°F. A few showers may brush Clemson and Central late Saturday night or early Sunday, but the favored western-fringe track keeps heavier coastal rain east. Saturday and Sunday confidence is lower because global guidance remains farther west, cooler and wetter.
upstate.confidence: High Friday; low-moderate Saturday and moderate Sunday because coastal-low track differences create a material cloud, temperature and rain spread even though the local spatial signal favors the western fringe

sourceNotes: OFFICIAL ALERTS: no active NWS point alert was present for Danville, Clemson or Central at the final issuance check. Official alerts remain separate from outlooks and this independent analysis.

The Louisville discussion supports sunshine and near-70°F temperatures Friday and Saturday, a cloudier upper-60s Sunday, and a light shower band with the cold front mainly Sunday evening or night. The dry column should keep rainfall to a few hundredths east of I-65.

Chris Bailey's November 20 Kentucky Weather Center post, ‘A Colder and More Active Setup For Thanksgiving Week,’ was accepted as authoritative published source material. Bailey forecasts 65–70°F through Sunday, with a few low-70s readings, followed by gusty showers with the late-Sunday cold front. Details absent from his post or unreadable in graphics were left unknown.

The Greenville-Spartanburg discussion raises late-Saturday-through-Sunday rain chances mainly in the eastern half of its area while explicitly retaining low track confidence. Clemson and Central are on the western fringe.

The Upstate conflict was resolved spatially, not ignored: current NWS point grids and RRFS/RDPS/GDPS favor a limited western-fringe brush, while ECMWF, GFS and especially GEFS are cooler and wetter. The candidate therefore uses 20–30% late-night rain chances, cool-side Saturday ranges and low-moderate weekend confidence.

The NHC 7 AM outlook places a broad low near central Florida with a 30% 48-hour and 50% seven-day formation chance. Coastal wind, surf, flooding and heavy-rain hazards remain east of the Clemson–Central corridor in the favored solution.
Official point guidance supports Danville near 67/39°F, 70/42°F and 68/45°F, and Clemson near 70/48°F, 66/51°F and 72/48°F.

COD CONUS radar at 13:30Z showed both inland corridors dry. GOES-19 visible imagery at 13:26Z showed the Ohio Valley largely free of thick cloud and the developing coastal system's expanding cloud shield off the Southeast coast.

Every currently available COD family was audited: HRRR, RAP, RRFS, GEM-RDPS, GEM-GDPS, ECMWF, GFS, AIFS, AIGFS, CFSv2, GEFS, REFS, AIFS-ENS and AIGEFS. NAM, NAM Nest, SREF and HiResW are retired; retained files were stale and excluded.

Fresh BUFKIT 19 GFS, HRRR, RAP and RRFS profiles were consulted. RRFS supports the western-fringe Upstate solution, while GFS BUFKIT is a much wetter and cooler west-track outlier. The newest validated local GRIB summary was more than 12 hours old and was excluded from weighting.
The maintained KDVK −1.5°F low correction and Kentucky empirical 5/5/6°F high and 8°F low widths were applied. Prose supplies one most-likely Danville value inside each calibrated range.
The maintained KCEU +1.5°F and KLQK −3°F low corrections preserve the Clemson–Central nighttime split inside current 10°F regional low ranges. Upstate high widths remain 4/5/6°F.
The latest completed accuracy summary contains 153 verified checkpoints across 53 forecasts and all-category accuracy of 81.1% overall, including 84.6% for Central Kentucky and 77.5% for the Upstate.
Current station corrections, empirical lead-specific widths, model records, calibrated confidence, explicit event windows and official-alert separation were applied.
All local times use Eastern Standard Time. The third card includes Sunday night and early Monday because validThrough is exactly 72 elapsed hours after issuance.
Contains modified ECMWF Open Data, selected and processed for independent forecast research under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0).
Tempest data was not used for Upstate observations, verification, calibration or adjustment.
This is a candidate only. No repository, forecast history, website, widget or publishing workflow was modified during preparation.
